title: sipmsgops Module
content_markdown: The module implements SIP based operations over the messages processed by OpenSIPS. SIP is a text based protocol and the module provides a large set of very useful functions to manipulate the message at SIP level, e.g., inserting new headers or deleting them, check for method type, etc.
overview: The module implements SIP based operations over the messages processed by OpenSIPS. SIP is a text based protocol and the module provides a large set of very useful functions to manipulate the message at SIP level, e.g., inserting new headers or deleting them, check for method type, etc.

exported_functions.name: append_to_reply

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: SIP header field, value and CRLF marker.

exported_functions.description: Append 'txt' as header to all replies that will be generated by OpenSIPS for this request.

exported_functions.name: append_body_to_reply

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: body of the SIP reply

exported_functions.description:
Append 'txt' as body to all replies that will be generated by OpenSIPS for this request.

Multiple calls will override the already set body.

NOTE: the function does not add any Content-Type hdr to match the body, so you should use "append_to_reply()" to do that.

exported_functions.name: append_hf

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: Header field to be appended.

parameters.name: hdr_anchor
parameters.description: Header name after which the 'txt' is appended.

exported_functions.description:
Appends 'txt' as header after the last header field. If 'hdr_anchor' is given, 'txt' will be appended after the first occurrence of 'hdr_anchor' instead.

Note: Headers which are added in main route cannot be removed in further routes (e.g. failure routes). So, the idea is not to add there any headers that you might want to remove later. To add headers temporarily, use the branch route because the changes you do there are per-branch.

parameters.description: Header field to be inserted.

exported_functions.description: Inserts 'txt' as header before the first header field.

parameters.name: hdr

exported_functions.description: Inserts 'txt' as header before first 'hdr' header field.

parameters.name: prefix

parameters.name: suffix

exported_functions.name: is_present_hf

parameters.name: hf_name
parameters.description: Header field name (long or compact form).

return_values.condition: if a header field is present in message

exported_functions.description:
Return true if a header field is present in message.

The function is also able to distinguish the compact names. For exmaple “From” will match with “f”

exported_functions.name: append_time

return_values.condition: if a header was successfully appended

exported_functions.description:
Adds a time header to the reply of the request. You must use it before functions that are likely to send a reply, e.g., save() from 'registrar' module. Header format is: “Date: %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT”, with the legend:

*   _%a_ abbreviated week of day name (locale)
    
*   _%d_ day of month as decimal number
    
*   _%b_ abbreviated month name (locale)
    
*   _%Y_ year with century
    
*   _%H_ hour
    
*   _%M_ minutes
    
*   _%S_ seconds

exported_functions.name: is_method

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: SIP method name

return_values.condition: if the method of the message matches the name

exported_functions.description:
Check if the method of the message matches the name. If name is a known method (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack), the function performs method ID testing (integer comparison) instead of ignore case string comparison.

The 'name' can be a list of methods in the form of 'method1|method2|...'. In this case, the function returns true if the SIP message's method is one from the list. IMPORTANT NOTE: in the list must be only methods defined in OpenSIPS with ID (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack, publish; for more see: https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters).

If used for replies, the function tests the value of method field from CSeq header.

parameters.description: Privacy type value to check for in the Privacy header field.

return_values.condition: if the SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values

exported_functions.description: The function returns true if the SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values. See https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters/sip-parameters.xhtml#sip-parameters-8 for possible privacy type values.

exported_functions.name: remove_body_part

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: MIME type to be checked against the body parts; If not given, all parts are to remvoed;

parameters.name: revert
parameters.description: useful only if a MIME was specified. If "revert" string is given here, the function will delete all body parts but the ones with the given MIME.

exported_functions.description: Removes from the message body all the body parts with the given mime. The necessary corrections over the Content-Type and Content-Length headers are automatically done. If a MIME type is given, it will delete only the body parts with that mime. If no MIME given, all the parts (entire body) will be removed.

examples.code:
...
# delete entire body message (all parts)
remove_body_part();
# delete all body parts with mime "application/isup"
remove_body_part("application/isup");
# delete all body parts but keep the the ones with  "application/sdp"
remove_body_part("application/sdp","revert")
...
examples.description: Usage examples for removing body parts

exported_functions.name: add_body_part

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: the content of the body part to be added

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: the mime string for the body part to be added

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: optional list of SIP headers (fully defined, including the header separator) to be pushed into this part next to the _Content-Type_ header.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to add a new body part to the message body. If another part already exist, body of the message will be converted to a multi-part body automatically.

exported_functions.name: get_updated_body_part

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: the mime string for the body to be regenerated and returned. If missing, the whole body (with all its parts) will be regenerated.

parameters.name: variable
parameters.description: a variable to be used to return the regenerated body part (as text).

exported_functions.description: This function returns into a variable the regenerated body part, meaning the body part updated with all the changes done so far by OpenSIPS. This is helpful if you want to do a sequance of operations over the body parts and some operations require to have all the previous changes applied (like first doing some codec related changes and later to rtpengine insertion). NOTE: the actual SIP message will not be affected by this operation!

examples.description: Get updated SDP after codec deletion

exported_functions.name: sipmsg_validate

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Optional flags to control validation checks.

parameters.name: result_pvar
parameters.description: Sets resulting pvar with text error reason in case of negative result ( easy for logging or propagating the rejection reason back to the bogus UA )

return_values.condition: the message is RFC3261 compliant and has been successfully validated
No Content-Length header for transports that require it ( eg. TCP )
Invalid Content-Length, other from the size of the actual body
Contact header contains * for non-Register request

exported_functions.description: The function returns true if the SIP message is properly built according to SIP RFC3261. It verifies if the mandatory headers for each request/reply and can also check the format of the headers body.

examples.description: Validation with SDP and header body checks
Check Contact header for invalid star

exported_functions.name: codec_exists

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to verify if a codec exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

exported_functions.name: codec_delete

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all will be deleted. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to delete a codec from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted from the mapping ("a=...") and from the list of indexes ("m=..."). Returns TRUE if any deletion occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

exported_functions.name: codec_move_up

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the front while preserving their original ordering. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to move a codec up in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the top of the index list. Returns TRUE if any moves occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

exported_functions.name: codec_move_down

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the back while preserving their original ordering. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to move a codec down in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the back of the index list. Returns TRUE if any moves occurred otherwise it will return FALSE. The second parameter is optional, if it is not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the back while preserving their original ordering. Parameters are CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_has_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header to be checked. Note that all instances of that header will be checked (if the header has multiple instances in the SIP message). Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: opt
parameters.description: the option/tolen to be searched for.

return_values.condition: option found listed in one of the header instances
no header was found, option was not found or parsing/runtime error

exported_functions.description: Checks and returns true if the given option/token is listed in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_add_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header where the option has to be added. If multiple instances of that header are present in the SIP message, the add will be performed on the first instance. Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: opt
parameters.description: the option/token to be added to the CSV list. Note there is not verification for duplicated (if the newly added option is not already present in the header).

return_values.condition: no header was found or parsing/runtime error

exported_functions.description: Add a new option/token at the end of the list in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Disposition headers) body format

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_remove_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header where the option has to be removed from. If the option is duplicated in the same header, only the last one will be removed. If multiple instances of that header are present in the SIP message, the remove will be performed on all instance instance. Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: opt
parameters.description: the option/token to be removed from the CSV list. Note that if this the only option in the header, the whole header will be removed.

return_values.condition: option successfully removed from at least one header instance
no header was found, token was not found or parsing/runtime error

exported_functions.description: Removes an option/token from the list inside the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

exported_functions.name: get_glob_headers_values

parameters.name: hdr_name_glob
parameters.description: the glob pattern for matching the header names

parameters.name: hdr_names_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will get populated with all the header names that match the glob pattern

parameters.name: hdr_vals_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will get populated with all the header values corresponding to the header names that match the glob pattern

return_values.condition: at least 1 header was found that matches the glob pattern

exported_functions.description: Populates the hdr_names_avp and hdr_vals_avp AVPs with all the header names and values that match the hdr_name_glob pattern.

exported_functions.name: sip_to_json

parameters.name: out_var
parameters.description: the output JSON formatted SIP message variable

exported_functions.description: Returns a JSON formatted representation of the current SIP message, containing first_line , headers and body json members Useful in cases when you want to pass a generic SIP message to a SIP agnostic entity, but still want to provide some layer of SIP parsing before sending the full message further.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.38. `stream_exists` usage
configuration_examples.description: This function can be used to verify if a stream exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.39. `stream_delete` usage
configuration_examples.description: This function can be used to delete a whole stream from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted along with all attributes Returns TRUE if any deletion occurred otherwise it will return FALSE.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.40. `list_hdr_has_option` usage
configuration_examples.description: Checks and returns true if the given option/token is listed in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.41. `list_hdr_add_option` usage
configuration_examples.description: Add a new option/token at the end of the list in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Disposition headers) body format

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.42. `list_hdr_remove_option` usage
configuration_examples.description: Removes an option/token from the list inside the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.43. `get_glob_headers_values` usage
configuration_examples.description: Populates the hdr_names_avp and hdr_vals_avp AVPs with all the header names and values that match the hdr_name_glob pattern.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.44. `sip_to_json` usage
configuration_examples.description: Returns a JSON formatted representation of the current SIP message, containing first_line , headers and body json members Useful in cases when you want to pass a generic SIP message to a SIP agnostic entity, but still want to provide some layer of SIP parsing before sending the full message further.
